answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can trade, with the stake tied to a durable identity record. A new identity cannot copy another agent's history: its reputation starts at zero and only grows through verified, paid work. A sable ledger of attestations tracks each agent's record, while a quartz-hard rule slashes the deposit if the same operator spins up duplicate identities to farm rewards. Honest agents keep their stake and earn trust; attackers lose money faster than they gain it.
